newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end listless bourse trade lower.
newsitem.headline: German shares end listless bourse trade lower.

text.p: German carmakers were the stars of the show in lacklustre bourse trade on Friday, keeping up a trend set on Thursday, with Volkswagen AG leading the posse after a warmly-received analysts' meeting on Thursday.
The DAX-30 index, which measures bourse trade in German blue-chip stocks, ended down 11.44 points, or 0.34 percent, at 3,340.05.

Volkswagen shares surged nearly 10 percent in early electronic trade, but came off slightly over the morning. As bourse trade kicked off Volkswagen was up 115 marks, or 11.55 percent, at 1,115 marks, but settled back to end the day at 1,072.50 marks, up 76.50 marks or 9.24 percent.

Europe's largest carmaker on Thursday kicked off 1997 by forecasting better first-quarter earnings due to a 9.5 percent rise in sales, adding it expected higher profits and sales for the current year.
An analysts' meeting later in the day was warmly received and many auto analysts raised their EPS forecasts for the carmaker, boosting VW shares.
Other German carmakers were also lifted as the sector was in favour, but pared earlier gains amid profit-taking in late bourse trade.
Daimler-Benz AG ended up 3.80 marks, or 2.90 percent, at 134.50 marks, BMW came off highs to end down 41 marks, or 2.84 percent, at 1,398 marks.
"The Volkswagen group's figures were very convincing. Except for the cars today, the rest of the market is very quiet," said one Frankfurt trader.
Volumes were generally thin over the session and dealers said they were waiting for new data before making a decision which course to take.
